tasks.short: Interview relevant parties to decide settlement, denial, or further review.

steps.what: Prepare claimant, witness, police, and physician questions

loop.input: claim chronology, missing evidence list, and contact roles
loop.check: claims adjuster removes leading or irrelevant questions before contact
loop.stop: stop when a party is vulnerable, represented, or a specialist is needed; prepare manually
loop.why_not_simpler: The questions must reflect the evidence gap and the role of each person.

steps.what: Interview or correspond with relevant claim parties
Evaluate interview evidence for settlement or denial
Record interview outcome and next claim action

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} case checklist prepares evidence-gap questions from the {OTHER} claim record. The claims adjuster conducts every interview, assesses the answers, and records the resulting settlement, denial, or review action.
tasks.previous_blocker: The decision rests on what people say, how it fits the evidence, and how a sensitive conversation is handled.
tasks.enabler_now: A checked question plan reduces preparation but does not replace the conversation or its assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, consent, distress, and disputed accounts remain human concerns.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster listens, adapts questions, and assesses meaning beyond the transcript.
tasks.altitude: Nothing material changes in decision rights; preparation is shorter and interview quality remains the focus.

reach.learn: Use neutral questions and a clear evidence trail.

evidence.claim: A bounded draft can prepare questions from a checked evidence gap, while the interview and decision stay human.

assumptions: The workflow begins with a missing or disputed fact and ends with a recorded next claim action.
Fields are claim identifier, party role, contact preference, evidence gap, question-plan version, contact outcome, and next action; the claims adjuster records them.
No conversation recording is used by default. The adjuster selects checked notes for the record.
One hour per 100 baseline hours covers question-template maintenance.
unknowns: Which contacts need consent, representation, or specialist handling.
Whether notes can be shared with a claims manager.
research_questions: How much preparation time is spent per contact?
Which evidence gaps recur by claim type?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Interviewing and assessment remain human work; one focal-role upkeep hour per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter claim payments, reserves, new claims, and sufficient file documentation.

steps.what: Validate payment, reserve, and new claim fields
Write validated claim payment and reserve records
Write concise sufficient claim file documentation

loop.input: approved claim-entry snapshot, checked evidence, and note template
loop.check: claims adjuster checks amounts, reasons, and the final snapshot before saving
loop.stop: stop on missing evidence or changed figures; write the note manually
loop.why_not_simpler: A sufficient note needs case-specific reasons, not only structured fields.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} claim record validates fields before an internal write creates a versioned payment, reserve, or new-claim snapshot. The claims adjuster approves that exact snapshot, then reviews a draft file note generated from checked evidence in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data is re-keyed between claim and finance records, while staff still need to explain the decision in the case file.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured validation and an internal interface can create a reviewable entry without sending money or changing a final record without approval.
tasks.still_hard: Reserve reasons, payment context, and documentation quality need an accountable claims adjuster.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster confirms that the recorded numbers represent the case and writes the reason a later reviewer needs.

ambition.what: Review a daily queue of failed claim-entry validations before they delay a payment or reserve update.

tasks.altitude: The role moves from re-keying routine values to reviewing exceptions and documentation quality.

reach.learn: Trace the approved claim-entry snapshot to the finance status.

evidence.claim: Configured field validation and an internal write can reduce duplicate claim entry while retaining human approval.

assumptions: The workflow begins with an approved payment, reserve change, or new claim and ends with a checked claim file note.
Fields are claim identifier, entry type, payment amount, reserve amount, currency, effective date, source version, reason code, and entry status; claims and finance teams provide them.
The internal write does not send a bank payment. Any field or source-version change voids approval of the snapshot.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours cover validation-rule updates and failed-entry review.
unknowns: Whether the claim and finance records support a versioned internal write.
Which entry types need a second approval.
research_questions: What share of entries are re-keyed today?
How often does a generated note need substantive correction?

already_counted.description: Approve claim-entry snapshots and review file notes

incremental.description: Maintain validation rules and review failed claim entries

approvals.approved_version: validated claim-entry pack version and claim-entry snapshot

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many validation failures and note corrections; three focal-role upkeep hours per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Resolve complex severe-exposure claims with high-service file handling.

steps.what: Triage severe exposure and assemble case timeline

loop.input: checked severe-claim records and dated notes
loop.output: case timeline with source links and open issues
loop.check: claims adjuster checks every material event against the file
loop.stop: stop on missing chronology or conflicting material facts; rebuild manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Severe claims have long, mixed histories and the material issues vary by case.

steps.what: Coordinate specialists, counsel, and service providers
Provide high-service updates to the claimant
Record severe-claim next actions and ownership

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} case view prepares a checked timeline and open-issue list from {OTHER} and {DOCS}. The claims adjuster coordinates specialists and supports the claimant directly, then records ownership and next actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: The valuable work is coordination, empathy, and judgement in a severe, evolving case, not a repeatable transaction.
tasks.enabler_now: A timeline and action record can reduce administrative reconstruction without displacing human service.
tasks.still_hard: Severe exposure, vulnerable people, and specialist decisions need a trusted accountable handler.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster builds trust, balances urgent needs, and keeps specialists aligned around a changing case.

ambition.what: Give every severe-claim claimant a clear named next action after each material update.

tasks.altitude: The role spends less time rebuilding the history and more time coordinating care, risk, and service.

reach.learn: Run a clear action log across specialist parties.

evidence.claim: A checked case timeline can prepare coordination work while high-service claim handling remains human.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a severe-exposure case is assigned and ends with a named action owner and next action.
Fields are claim identifier, severity reason, event date, issue, action owner, due date, specialist status, and claimant contact preference; the claims adjuster records them.
No automated claimant communication is sent. One hour per 100 baseline hours covers timeline and action-template upkeep.
unknowns: Which claim criteria define severe exposure.
Which specialists may access the case timeline.
research_questions: How often is case history reconstructed manually?
Which action records are needed by specialists?

already_counted.description: Review the severe-claim timeline and action record

incremental.description: Maintain severe-claim timeline fields and action templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most time remains in specialist coordination and claimant service; one focal-role upkeep hour per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adjust reserves or recommend reserves consistent with corporate policy.

steps.what: Assemble claim exposure, payment, and reserve history
Calculate reserve movement and policy variance
Judge reserve adequacy and make recommendation
Record reserve adjustment rationale and evidence

tasks.design: A scheduled view in {OTHER} assembles reserve history and payment data from {ERP}, then calculates the movement against the reserve policy in {DOCS}. The claims adjuster judges adequacy, makes any recommendation, and records the rationale.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reserve decisions require case context even where the underlying history and arithmetic are structured.
tasks.enabler_now: A joined reserve-review pack and visible policy variance remove manual assembly and recalculation.
tasks.still_hard: Future exposure, new evidence, and an adequate reserve remain financial judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The claims adjuster interprets changing evidence and the commercial consequence of holding too much or too little reserve.

ambition.what: Review material reserve variances daily instead of waiting for a periodic file review.

tasks.altitude: The role spends less time assembling history and more time challenging reserve assumptions and portfolio patterns.

reach.learn: Separate historical movement from case-specific exposure judgement.

evidence.claim: Structured history can be joined and arithmetic checked before an adjuster makes a reserve judgement.

assumptions: The workflow starts with a reserve review and ends with a documented reserve recommendation or adjustment rationale.
Fields are claim identifier, current reserve, prior reserve, payment history, exposure category, policy threshold, evidence date, and recommendation reason; claims and finance systems provide them.
The system calculates only from supplied history. It does not change a reserve or publish a recommendation without a human decision.
One hour per 100 baseline hours covers threshold maintenance and variance-check exceptions.
unknowns: Which reserve policies and thresholds can be represented as rules.
Who has authority to approve a reserve adjustment.
research_questions: What share of reserve reviews have a simple policy variance?
How often does new evidence reverse a recommendation?

already_counted.description: Review reserve history and the calculated variance

incremental.description: Maintain reserve thresholds and review variance exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Reserve adequacy and the final rationale remain human work; one focal-role upkeep hour per 100 baseline hours is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Focus on disputed evidence, severe-claim service, and reserve judgement rather than reconstructing histories and re-keying records.
reach: Support finance with versioned claim-entry exception evidence.
Support analysts with checked reserve-movement context.
role.ambitious_version: A claims team that catches data and evidence gaps earlier while retaining human judgement over claimant conversations, severe exposure, payments, and reserves.
